vulnerabilities.title: SHELLCODE_FILTER_BYPASS_VIA_NUL_BYTE_AND_STRLEN

root_cause.description: The is_all_upper function uses strlen(buf) as the loop bound for byte filtering. strlen stops scanning at the first NUL (0x00) byte. However, the shellcode buffer is populated by read(0, buf, 99), which performs raw binary I/O and does NOT stop at NUL bytes. An attacker can inject a NUL byte early in the input (e.g., position 1), causing strlen to return a small value (e.g., 1). The filter then only checks bytes before the NUL byte, leaving all bytes after the NUL completely unfiltered. These unfiltered bytes are still present in the RWX mmap buffer and are executed via 'call rax' at 0x401b4b. This completely bypasses the byte filter security control, allowing arbitrary shellcode (including syscall instructions 0x0f 0x05, int 0x80, etc.) to be placed after the NUL byte and executed.

data_flow: stdin -> read(0, mmap_buf, 99) at 0x4019ad
read stores raw bytes including NUL (0x00) into mmap_buf
newline replacement: if buf[read_ret-1]==0x0a, set to 0x00 (only last byte)
is_all_upper(mmap_buf) called at 0x401a07
is_all_upper loop bound = strlen(mmap_buf) at 0x4018c4
strlen stops at first NUL byte in buffer
only bytes [0..strlen-1] are checked against filter
bytes [strlen..read_ret-1] are NOT checked
main executes call rax (0x401b4b) jumping to mmap_buf
entire buffer (including unfiltered bytes after NUL) is executed

security_check.expected: All bytes in the shellcode buffer (up to read_ret bytes) should be validated against the allowed byte set {0x20, 0x30-0x39, 0x41-0x5a}
security_check.actual: Only bytes up to the first NUL byte (as determined by strlen) are validated. Bytes after the first NUL byte are not checked at all.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: The filter uses strlen(buf) as loop bound instead of the actual number of bytes read (read return value). strlen is a string function that stops at NUL, but the input is binary data from read() which can contain NUL bytes. The correct approach would be to iterate over read_ret bytes, not strlen(buf) bytes.

vulnerable_operation.operation: indirect call to user-controlled RWX memory with incomplete filter
vulnerable_operation.size: up to 99 bytes (read size), but only strlen(buf) bytes filtered

impact.reason: Arbitrary unfiltered bytes are placed in RWX memory and executed as machine instructions. The attacker controls the instruction stream, which can include any x86-64 instruction (syscall, mov, xor, etc.) by placing them after a NUL byte. This allows arbitrary code execution within the process. No seccomp/sandbox is present (S1 F013), so the shellcode has full syscall access.
If the filter bypass is used to inject invalid or unintended instructions, the process may crash with SIGSEGV or SIGILL. However, the attacker can also inject valid shellcode that does not crash.

evidence.description: is_all_upper calls strlen(buf) at 0x4018c4 to determine the loop bound. The comparison at 0x4018c9 (cmp rbx, rax) checks i < strlen(buf). strlen stops at the first NUL byte, so only bytes before the first NUL are filtered.
main calls read(0, mmap_buf, 99) at 0x4019ad. read() performs raw binary I/O and does not stop at NUL bytes. The user can inject NUL (0x00) bytes anywhere in the 99-byte input.
After is_all_upper passes, main executes 'call rax' at 0x401b4b where rax = mmap_buf (0x13370000). The entire buffer content (including unfiltered bytes after NUL) is executed as machine code.

main calls memset(mmap_buf, 0, 100) at 0x40197c before read. This zeroes the buffer, but read() overwrites bytes with user input including potential NUL bytes. The memset does not prevent the NUL injection bypass.

The filter loop iterates i from 0 to strlen(buf)-1. If buf = [0x41, 0x00, 0x48, 0x31, 0xc0, 0x0f, 0x05], strlen returns 1, so only buf[0]=0x41 (uppercase A) is checked and passes. Bytes 0x00, 0x48, 0x31, 0xc0, 0x0f, 0x05 (which include 'xor eax,eax' and 'syscall') are not checked but are executed.

verification_required: Confirm that read() on stdin can receive NUL bytes (e.g., via pipe with binary data)
Verify that is_all_upper returns 1 (pass) when input contains a NUL byte after a valid byte
Confirm that call rax executes bytes after the NUL byte (not just up to it)
Determine if CET/IBT is enforced at runtime (if enforced, call rax to non-endbr64 target may fault, but the filter bypass still exists structurally)

vulnerabilities.title: READ_RETURN_VALUE_INSUFFICIENT_CHECK

root_cause.description: The return value of read(0, mmap_buf, 99) is checked with 'cmp DWORD PTR [rbp-0xac], 0x0; jne' at 0x4019b8-0x4019bf, which only rejects a return value of exactly 0 (EOF). A negative return value (read returns -1 on error) is non-zero and passes the check. The code then uses the return value as an index: buf[read_ret - 1]. When read_ret = -1, this computes buf[-2], which is an out-of-bounds access at mmap_buf - 2 (address 0x1336FFFE), before the mmap region. If the byte at that address happens to be 0x0a (newline), the code writes 0x00 to buf[-2], constituting an out-of-bounds write.

attack_surface.input: read() return value (error condition on stdin)
data_flow: read(0, mmap_buf, 99) at 0x4019ad returns -1 on error
return value stored as int32 at [rbp-0xac] at 0x4019b2
check: cmp [rbp-0xac], 0x0; jne -> -1 != 0, passes check
eax = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) at 0x4019d0
cdqe sign-extends to 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at 0x4019d6
lea rdx, [rax-1] -> rdx = -2 (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE) at 0x4019d8
rax = mmap_buf + rdx = 0x13370000 - 2 = 0x1336FFFE at 0x4019e0
movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rax] -> OOB read at 0x1336FFFE at 0x4019e3
if byte == 0x0a: mov BYTE PTR [rax], 0x00 -> OOB write at 0x1336FFFE at 0x4019fd

security_check.expected: read() return value should be checked for <= 0 (both EOF and error) to reject negative returns
security_check.actual: read() return value is only checked for == 0 (EOF only). Negative returns (errors) pass the check.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing check for negative return value. The comparison should be 'if (read_ret <= 0) abort' instead of 'if (read_ret == 0) abort'.

vulnerable_operation.operation: out-of-bounds memory access using unchecked negative read return value as index
vulnerable_operation.target: address 0x1336FFFE (2 bytes before mmap region at 0x13370000)

impact.reason: When read() returns -1, the code reads a byte at mmap_buf - 2 (0x1336FFFE), which is outside the 100-byte mmap region. This address may be unmapped (causing SIGSEGV) or may contain data from an adjacent memory region.

If the OOB-read byte at 0x1336FFFE equals 0x0a (newline), the code writes 0x00 to that address (0x1336FFFE), which is an out-of-bounds write of 1 NUL byte before the mmap region. This could corrupt adjacent memory metadata or data.
If address 0x1336FFFE is unmapped, the OOB read causes SIGSEGV, crashing the process.

evidence.description: read return value checked with 'cmp DWORD PTR [rbp-0xac], 0x0; jne 0x4019d0'. This only rejects return value == 0 (EOF). A return value of -1 (error) is non-zero and passes the check.

After the check passes with read_ret=-1, cdqe at 0x4019d6 sign-extends eax (0xFFFFFFFF) to rax (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF). Then lea rdx, [rax-1] computes rdx = -2. Adding to mmap_buf (0x13370000) yields 0x1336FFFE, which is before the mmap region.
movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rax] reads a byte from address 0x1336FFFE (OOB read). If this byte equals 0x0a, mov BYTE PTR [rax], 0x00 at 0x4019fd writes NUL to 0x1336FFFE (OOB write).

verification_required: Determine if read() on stdin can be made to return -1 in an attacker-controllable way (e.g., closing stdin, sending signal causing EINTR)
Check if address 0x1336FFFE is mapped at runtime (adjacent to mmap region or unmapped)
Verify whether the OOB write (if triggered) corrupts any security-relevant data

vulnerabilities.title: REGISTER_STATE_INFORMATION_LEAK_BEFORE_SHELLCODE_EXECUTION

root_cause.description: Before executing the user-controlled shellcode via call rax, main saves all general-purpose registers (rax, rbx, rcx, rdx, rbp, rsp, rsi, rdi, r8-r13) to the stack and prints them to stdout via _IO_printf at 0x401afb. This leaks runtime stack addresses (rsp, rbp) and libc data segment addresses (rbx points near libc data) to the shellcode. Since the binary has No PIE (fixed base 0x400000) but the stack and libc addresses are subject to ASLR, this information leak provides ASLR bypass information that the shellcode can use.

attack_surface.input: register state printed to stdout before shellcode execution
data_flow: main saves registers to stack at 0x401a46-0x401a85
main calls _IO_printf with format string at 0x498070 to print all registers at 0x401afb
register values (including rsp, rbp, rbx) are written to stdout
shellcode can read stdout or the printed values are available to the attacker
shellcode executes with knowledge of stack and libc addresses

security_check.expected: Register state should not be leaked to the shellcode/attacker before execution, as it provides ASLR bypass information
security_check.actual: All register values are printed to stdout before call rax
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: No attempt to hide or randomize register state before shellcode execution. The register dump is an intentional feature of the challenge but constitutes an information leak.

vulnerable_operation.operation: information leak via printf of register state
vulnerable_operation.expression: _IO_printf(format_string, rax, rbx, rcx, rdx, rbp, rsp, rsi, rdi, r8, r9, r10, r11, r12, r13)

impact.reason: Stack addresses (rsp, rbp) and libc data segment addresses (rbx) are printed to stdout before shellcode execution. This provides ASLR bypass information. Combined with the filter bypass (BUG-001), the shellcode can use these addresses to construct ROP chains or direct syscalls with correct addresses.

evidence.description: main calls _IO_printf at 0x401afb with format string at 0x498070, printing all register values (rax through r13) to stdout before executing call rax.
main saves all registers to stack at 0x401a46-0x401a85, then restores them at 0x401b04-0x401b43 before call rax. The register state is available to the shellcode at execution time.

S1 runtime fact F012 confirms register state leaked at runtime includes stack address (rsp/rbp) and libc data segment addresses (rbx), providing ASLR bypass info. S1 runtime fact F011 confirms different stack addresses across runs (0x7ffe... vs 0x7fff... vs 0x7ffd...) suggesting ASLR is on, making this leak significant.

verification_required: Confirm which specific register values are printed and whether they include stack and libc addresses
Verify that the printed values are accurate and usable for ASLR bypass

non_vulnerabilities.description: init sets stdin/stdout/stderr to unbuffered (setvbuf _IONBF) and calls alarm(60). No security issues found.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: setvbuf with _IONBF is standard practice for CTF challenges. alarm(60) provides a timeout but is not a vulnerability.

non_vulnerabilities.description: _abort prints a message via printf and calls exit(1). No security issues found.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: Simple error handling function with no user-controlled format string or buffer operations.

non_vulnerabilities.description: mmap return value check: cmp [rbp-0x40], -1; jne. This correctly checks for mmap failure (returns -1 on error).
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The mmap return value is properly checked against -1 (MAP_FAILED). If mmap fails, _abort is called. This is correct error handling.

non_vulnerabilities.description: memset(mmap_buf, 0, 100) before read ensures the buffer is zero-initialized.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The memset prevents use of uninitialized memory in the buffer. However, it does not prevent the NUL byte bypass (BUG-001) because read() overwrites the zeroed bytes with user input that can contain NUL bytes.

non_vulnerabilities.description: Stack canary check at 0x401b52-0x401b61: compares fs:0x28 with saved canary, calls __stack_chk_fail on mismatch.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: Stack canary is properly implemented. However, the primary vulnerability (BUG-001) does not involve stack buffer overflow - it involves shellcode execution in the mmap region, which is not protected by the stack canary.

unresolved.reason: The binary has GNU property IBT,SHSTK marked in .note.gnu.property. If IBT is enforced by the kernel, 'call rax' to the mmap buffer (which does not start with endbr64) would cause a #CP fault, preventing shellcode execution. S1 runtime test showed SIGSEGV for 'AAAA' input, but this could be due to invalid instructions (0x41 0x41 0x41 0x41 = REX prefixes with no valid instruction) rather than IBT enforcement.
unresolved.required_next_step: S3 should dynamically verify whether IBT is enforced by testing 'call rax' to a buffer starting with endbr64 (0xf3 0x0f 0x1e 0xfa) followed by a NOP sled. If IBT is enforced, the filter bypass (BUG-001) still exists structurally but shellcode execution may be blocked unless the shellcode starts with endbr64 (which requires bytes 0xf3, 0x0f, 0x1e, 0xfa - none of which are in the allowed set, but could be placed after a NUL byte via BUG-001).

unresolved.description: ASLR status of the runtime environment
unresolved.reason: S1 could not confirm ASLR status from static analysis. S1 runtime observations showed varying stack addresses across runs, suggesting ASLR is on. The binary itself has No PIE (fixed base 0x400000), but stack and libc addresses may be randomized.
unresolved.required_next_step: S3 should confirm ASLR status. If ASLR is on, the register leak (BUG-003) provides necessary bypass information. If ASLR is off, the leak is less critical.

unresolved.description: Whether mmap returns exactly 0x13370000 at runtime
unresolved.reason: mmap is called with hint address 0x13370000. The kernel may honor or ignore this hint. S1 runtime showed rax=0x13370000 printed, suggesting the hint is honored, but this was not definitively confirmed.
unresolved.required_next_step: S3 should verify the mmap return address is consistently 0x13370000 across runs.
